speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; please describe the onset and characteristics of these symptoms in detail.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The recent camping trip in Minnesota and history of self-resolving knee pain raise concerns for Lyme disease; has the knee pain been recurrent or associated with a rash like "bull's eye"? To assess the wrist infection, I will need to check your vitals and examine the joint. REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Arthritis.

The Gram-negative diplococci in your wrist fluid and positive STI screen confirm a gonococcal infection. The skin lesions and history of joint pain are classic for the migratory arthritis-dermatitis syndrome of this disease. Please confirm if the "camping trip" and "Minnesota" details were part of a separate health history or if you suspect a different travel-related illness like Lyme disease.
